groups.title: Soft Capsule (D65200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E78000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins B1, B2, B6 and D in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age, for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and for beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium (an excess of calcium in the blood) or kidney stones; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are being given a cardiac glycoside; if you have kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 1 month or more, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an intravenous lipid preparation, an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, becoming heavier or bleeding for longer occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose. Do not take 2 tablets or more within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to other H2 receptor antagonists; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have difficulty taking it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 15 years or younger; if you have unexplained weight loss or persistent abdominal pain; if you have kidney disease; or if you are on haemodialysis.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another stomach medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol, chloroquine, a tetracycline antibiotic, diflunisal, digoxin, a diphosphonate, fexofenadine, iron (salts), a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, sodium fluoride, a glucocorticoid, indometacin, ketoconazole, lansoprazole, a phenothiazine antiepileptic, penicillamine, a phosphate, thyroxine or a salicylate.

Rarely anaphylaxis, enzyme abnormalities, constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, flatulence (abdominal distension), vomiting, thirst, rash, itching, urticaria, peeling of the skin, fatigue, jaundice, hepatitis, angioneurotic oedema, joint pain or muscle cramps, and occasionally nausea, diarrhoea or headache may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (172836ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) per dose. Ages 7 to 10 years: take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) per dose. Ages 3 to 6 years: take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) per dose. Ages 1 to 2 years: take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) per dose. Take it 3 to 4 times in 1 day. A child weighing less than 30 kg must not be given more than 500 mg (25 mL) in 1 day, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are breast-feeding; if you are being given high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Do not take more than the recommended dose. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or another condition listed in the approved product information.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or an anaphylactic reaction, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots; visual disturbance, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral oedema.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness and in old age, and for neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; if you have had an allergic reaction to soybean oil; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are being given a cardiac glycoside; if you are short of folic acid; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you are at particular risk from fat overload.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 1 month or more, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cardiac glycoside, an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, diarrhoea, stomatitis, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, dizziness, swelling of the face or legs, erythema, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or oedema and fluid retention occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E69900ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age who has had, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); or if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease or diabetes.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with another medicine.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body or on the mouth or eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.usage: Adults: take 0.5 to 1 tablet (50 to 100 mg) per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

If, rarely, rash, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or stomach pain occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is really necessary; if you have a constitution prone to allergy or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (260300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a nasal cold and by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose. Children (aged 12 to 14 years): take 1/2 tablet per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, after each meal.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe liver or kidney impairment; if you have severe coronary heart disease; if you have difficulty passing urine with residual urine; if you have high blood pressure or coronary artery disease; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby aged 2 years or younger; if you are being given an MAO inhibitor; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or if you have asthma, glaucoma, heart disease, arrhythmia, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia.

Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor, a blood-pressure-lowering medicine, alcohol, a central nervous system depressant (hypnotic, sedative, tranquilliser), a sympathomimetic, a tricyclic antidepressant, guanethidine, bretylium, bethanidine, debrisoquine, methyldopa, a sympathomimetic medicine (decongestant, appetite suppressant, amphetamine-type stimulant) or an alpha or beta adrenergic blocker.

If sedation, drowsiness, central nervous system depression, central stimulation, anxiety, sweating, a mild fall in blood pressure, visual disturbance, dilated pupils, delirium, hallucination, excitement, muscle cramps, stiffness, athetosis, clonic and tonic convulsions, high fever, respiratory paralysis, coma, circulatory paralysis, skin reactions, temporary stinging pain, a burning sensation, thirst, nausea, vomiting, difficulty passing urine, excitement, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, fever, erythema, many small pustules or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E20200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, toothache, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it (rash, reddening of the skin, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic (a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic) or a cold medicine has caused or may cause an asthma attack; if you have peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment or reduced heart function; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have or have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine); or if the user is a child.

Children and older people should take the smallest necessary amount and watch for adverse reactions. Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, adults must not take it for pain for 10 days or more and children must not take it for 5 days or more, and it must not be taken for fever for 3 days or more; in particular, watch the condition carefully after taking it in children and older people with a high fever and in people with a wasting disease. If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if a new symptom appears, consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, rash, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), severe symptoms with high fever such as rash, reddening of the skin and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (142334ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 months and older: take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight (5 to 7 mg per kg) per dose at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, without exceeding 4 doses (28 mg per kg) in 1 day. For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma, or asthma, urticaria or an allergy caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if any of the conditions listed in the approved product information apply to you.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a sulfonylurea, a diuretic with an antihypertensive, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like), chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure; aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; triggering of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash or itching; rarely loss of vision or visual disturbance such as scotoma; aseptic meningitis; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, or high blood potassium.

Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or swelling around the eye sockets, rarely jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or ALP, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude or acute pulmonary oedema, and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, constipation, malaise, fever or nosebleed may occur; if these occur, consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (149801ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the treatment of insomnia and for sedation.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (25 mg), 1 time in 1 day, always 30 minutes before sleep. The dose may be increased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a breathing disorder such as emphysema, chronic bronchitis or asthma; if you have glaucoma or prostatic hyperplasia; if you are breast-feeding; or if the user is a child aged 15 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Excessive sedation may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it for 2 weeks or more without consulting a doctor or pharmacist.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with an imipramine-type antidepressant, an anti-Parkinson medicine or disopyramide. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Anticholinergic effects may occur from time to time.

groups.title: Tablet (D04600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and relief of dizziness, vomiting and headache caused by motion sickness.
groups.usage: To prevent motion sickness, take it 30 minutes to 1 hour before travelling: those aged 15 years and older take 1 tablet per dose; ages 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 tablet per dose; ages 8 years to under 11 years take 1/2 tablet per dose. If a further dose is taken when symptoms appear, take the same amount again, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, and take it no more than 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; or if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with another anti-emetic, a cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, an antihistamine, a sedative, an antitussive-expectorant or an alcoholic drink.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching or palpitations occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
